title: What Data Tools Improve Lender Matching? A Practical Guide
summary: Data aggregation, cash-flow data, automated decisioning, fraud checks, and multi-lender routing improve matching. They send each deal to best-fit lenders.
body_markdown:
### What Data Tools Improve Lender Matching?


The best data tools for lender matching are data aggregation, real-time credit and cash-flow data, automated decisioning, fraud checks, and multi-lender orchestration with decline waterfalls. Used together, they build one complete borrower profile and send it to the lenders most likely to approve it.


Lender matching is the process of pairing a business loan application with a lender whose credit rules fit that borrower. In Lendflow's view, good matching means routing a complete, verified profile to the right lender, so a single credit score is only one input.


Many applicants still walk away short. In the[Fed Small Business Credit Survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/2026-report-on-employer-firms) , 42% of applicants received the full amount they sought, 36% received some or most, and 22% received none. The Fed drew these figures from a convenience sample of survey respondents, so they describe that sample rather than every U.S. small business.


[Lendflow's platform results](https://www.lendflow.com/post/fintech-infrastructure) report over $1.5B in offers made on its platform and an average of 42% faster speed to funding for pre-qualified offers. The sections below explain each tool, starting with where borrower data comes from.


### Unify Borrower Data in One Place


Data aggregation means collecting a borrower's information from many sources and combining it into one profile. When every lender reviews the same facts, decisions stay consistent and borrowers don't have to send the same paperwork twice.


Skip the spreadsheet shuffle and use a[data aggregation platform for lenders](https://www.lendflow.com/post/what-a-data-aggregation-platform-does-for-lenders) to connect each source once and reuse the profile everywhere. That page notes Lendflow Connect ships widgets in under two weeks and delivers a full API in 30 to 45 days. A typical profile pulls from five kinds of data:


- **Bank data:** Shows deposits, balances, and spending patterns that reveal how cash moves through the business.
- **Credit data:** Adds business bureau history and the personal credit history of each owner.
- **Accounting data:** Confirms revenue, expenses, and unpaid invoices straight from the books.
- **Identity data:** Ties the application to a real person and a registered business.
- **Document data:** Turns tax returns, statements, and IDs into fields a system can read.


Data orchestration is the layer above aggregation, and it controls the order in which data is pulled, cleaned, and sent to each tool or lender. Lendflow Connect and Data Graph handle this layer, so lenders can connect with top integration partners in minutes instead of building each connection by hand.


#### Pull Real-Time Credit Signals Through APIs


Real-time data is information pulled at the moment you need it. Batch data is pulled on a set schedule, such as monthly, so it can be weeks old when a lender reads it.


An API (application programming interface) is a connection that lets one system request data from another system automatically. A[real-time credit data API](https://www.lendflow.com/post/credit-data-api) pulls bureau and bank data on demand, so each lender sees current numbers at decision time. Lendflow's platform supports live credit signals and workflows that adapt as new data flows in.


### Look Past the Credit Score With Cash-Flow Data


Cash-flow data is the record of money moving in and out of a business bank account. Cash-flow underwriting uses that record to judge whether a business can repay, alongside its owner's credit score. It's one of the most useful types of alternative credit data, which means any data that sits outside a traditional credit report.


In the[FinRegLab cash-flow underwriting study](https://finreglab.org/press-releases/finreglab-study-shows-cash-flow-data-can-expand-small-business-lending/) , models adding cash-flow variables to personal credit scores and traditional inputs predicted default risk more accurately for every segment. The study covered more than 38,000 loans from two fintech lenders, made between 2015 and 2024.


The biggest gains showed up for low-score owners of businesses less than five years old, a group that credit scores alone often misjudge. Because the results come from two fintech lenders, test any cash-flow model against your own loan data before you rely on it. The U.S. Commerce Department's Minority Business Development Agency funded the research, and Visa and Plaid supported data connectivity.


Input What it shows Where it falls short


Personal credit score The owner's past borrowing and repayment habits Says little about how the business earns cash today


Business bureau data Trade lines and payment history with suppliers Often thin or missing for young businesses


Cash-flow (bank) data Recent deposits, balances, and spending Needs borrower consent and clean transaction categories


### Decide Faster With Automated Credit Decisioning


Automated credit decisioning is software that reviews an application and applies lending rules without a person handling each step by hand. It usually runs four steps in order: collect the data, verify it, score the risk, and apply the lender's policy.


Predictive modeling, which uses past loan data to estimate future risk, often powers the scoring step. For a full walkthrough, see[how automated credit decisioning works](https://www.lendflow.com/post/how-automated-credit-decisioning-works) . Each decision ends in one of four outcomes:


- **Approve:** The profile meets the lender's policy, and an offer goes out to the borrower.
- **Decline:** The profile misses key rules, and the deal can move to the next lender.
- **Refer:** The file goes to a human underwriter who reviews the edge cases.
- **Counteroffer:** The lender approves a different amount or term than the borrower requested.


Lendflow Intelligence runs this decisioning layer as a real-time insights engine that applies each lender's rules to the same profile. Lendflow Automate adds AI agents such as Doc Analyzer and Trust Score to handle document review and verification work, freeing underwriters for judgment calls.


#### Use AI Where It Adds Real Signal


AI is a tool, and adding more of it does not guarantee better lending outcomes. It works best on narrow jobs like reading documents or spotting unusual patterns, while people keep the final say on hard cases.


The[San Francisco Fed AI study](https://www.frbsf.org/research-and-insights/publications/economic-letter/2026/09/how-ai-adoption-might-affect-bank-lending/) found high-AI banks hold a much smaller average share of SME loans than low-AI banks, at 12% versus 21%. SME stands for small and midsize enterprises. The authors note the results are correlations, cover banks only, and measure AI through AI-related job postings rather than actual use.


### Stop Bad Matches With Fraud and Identity Checks


A bad match can mean a wrong lender, and it can also mean a fake borrower. Fraud checks confirm that the person and the business behind an application are real before any lender spends time on the file.


Personally identifiable information (PII) means details such as names, birth dates, addresses, and Social Security numbers. A[Federal Reserve synthetic identity fraud](https://fedpaymentsimprovement.org/news/blog/what-is-real-how-ai-is-transforming-synthetic-identity-fraud/) explainer defines it as combining PII to fabricate a person or entity for personal or financial gain. The word "entity" matters here, because fraudsters can invent a fake business as easily as a fake person.


- **Identity verification:** Confirms the applicant is a real person whose details match their ID and records.
- **Business verification:** Checks that the company is registered, active, and tied to the person applying.
- **Document analysis:** Flags altered bank statements or figures that don't match across uploaded files.


### Route Every Deal With Multi-Lender Orchestration


Multi-lender orchestration checks one borrower profile against many lenders' criteria at once and routes the deal to the best fits.


Loan routing is the act of sending an application to a specific lender, and orchestration decides where each deal goes. Skip one-lender dead ends and use orchestration to send each deal where its profile fits. Routing logic typically weighs four factors:


- **Credit profile:** Compares owner and business credit history against each lender's minimums.
- **Industry:** Accounts for lenders that favor or avoid certain types of businesses.
- **Revenue:** Checks monthly deposits and annual sales against each lender's floor.
- **Loan amount and type:** Matches the requested size and product, such as a term loan or line of credit.

For setup advice, read our[multi-lender orchestration best practices](https://www.lendflow.com/post/multi-lender-orchestration-guide) .


#### Recover Declined Deals With Waterfalls


A decline waterfall is a setup where a declined application automatically moves to the next lender in line, without the borrower applying again. Lenders are usually ordered by credit appetite, starting with prime lenders that offer the best rates and ending with alternative lenders.


Consent has to come first, which means the borrower agrees up front to share data with every lender in the waterfall. Lendflow's Second-Look Marketplace gives declined borrowers a path to other lenders, so fewer deals leave money on the table. Our[credit waterfall guide](https://www.lendflow.com/post/credit-waterfall) walks through each step and notes that Lendflow Connect reaches 75+ specialty and bank lenders through a single integration.


### Keep Lender Matching Explainable and Compliant


Explainability means you can say in plain words why a model approved or declined someone. Bias testing checks whether outcomes differ unfairly across groups of applicants, and it should run before and after a model goes live.


- **Fairness testing:** Compares approval rates and terms across applicant groups to find gaps worth investigating.
- **Reason codes:** Records the specific factors behind each decline in words a borrower can understand.
- **Audit trails:** Logs every data pull, routing step, lender response, and consent event for later review.


ECOA is the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, and Regulation B is the rule that carries it out. In 2022,[CFPB Circular 2022-03](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2022/06/14/2022-12729/consumer-financial-protection-circular-2022-03-adverse-action-notification-requirements-in) said a creditor cannot justify ECOA and Regulation B noncompliance because its technology "is too complicated or opaque to understand."


The[CFPB withdrawn guidance list](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/compliance/guidance/withdrawn-guidance/) shows that Circular 2022-03 was withdrawn on May 12, 2025, while the Bureau reviews its guidance. Check your current obligations with legal counsel before you change how your models explain decisions.


Open banking rules are also in flux, and they affect how lenders access bank data with a borrower's permission. As of January 2026, the[CFPB personal financial data rights](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/compliance/compliance-resources/other-applicable-requirements/personal-financial-data-rights/) page says a court stayed the Section 1033 rule's compliance dates on October 29, 2025. The CFPB is also reconsidering that rule, so check with legal counsel before you build matching workflows around either item.


### How to Choose Data Tools for Lender Matching


Start with the gap that costs you the most deals, and then pick the data tools for lender matching that close it. The table below pairs each category with what it improves and a question to ask any vendor.


Tool category What it improves Question to ask vendors


Data aggregation One consistent borrower profile Which bank, credit, and accounting sources connect out of the box?


Real-time credit data API Current data at decision time How fresh is each data pull, and what does each call cost?


Cash-flow underwriting Clearer views of young or low-score businesses Has the model been tested on loans like ours?


Automated decisioning Faster, more consistent decisions Can our team edit rules without engineering help?


Fraud and identity checks Fewer fake or altered applications Does it verify both the person and the business?


Multi-lender orchestration Better lender fit and recovered declines How many lenders are live, and how is consent captured?


Explainability tools Clear reasons and audit trails Can we export reason codes and logs for review?


Next, decide between point solutions and a unified platform. A point solution is a single-purpose tool you connect yourself, while a unified platform bundles data, decisioning, and routing together.


- **Point solutions:** Offer depth in one area but add integrations, contracts, and data handoffs to manage.
- **Unified platform:** Shares one profile across every step and cuts integration work, with less freedom to swap parts.


Good matching also means setting honest borrower expectations about cost. The[2025 SBCS employer firms report](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/2026-report-on-employer-firms) found 60% of respondents who borrowed from online lenders said costs were higher than expected. Show the total cost clearly in every offer, and see our guide to[data-driven loan placement](https://www.lendflow.com/post/data-driven-loan-placement) for a full placement framework.


### Lender Matching FAQs


#### What are alternatives to credit scores for lender matching?


Cash-flow data from business bank accounts is the most common alternative, along with accounting records, business bureau data, and verified documents like tax returns. These inputs show how a business runs today, which helps when an owner's credit score tells only part of the story.


#### How can lenders check for bias in loan approvals?


Lenders can compare approval rates and terms across applicant groups, review the reason codes behind declines, and keep audit trails of every decision. Compliance counsel should review the testing method and any gaps it uncovers.


#### Will AI replace loan officers and brokers?


AI agents can take over repetitive tasks such as document review, data entry, and borrower follow-ups. Loan officers and brokers still handle relationships, judgment calls, and complex deals that models can't settle alone.


#### What KPIs should a lending dashboard show?


A lending dashboard should track key performance indicators (KPIs) like application volume, approval rate by lender, time to decision, and speed to funding. Adding decline recovery, offer acceptance, and default rates shows whether faster matches also produce healthy loans.


#### Is a credit waterfall the same as a decline waterfall?


In most usage, yes, because both describe an application moving from one lender to the next until one approves it. "Credit waterfall" usually names the whole tiered lender structure, while "decline waterfall" stresses what happens after a lender says no.
